title: Do not cut benefits for disabled young people, dozens of UK charities urge ministers
content: More than 40 of the UK's leading charities have warned ministers against imposing tougher benefit sanctions or cuts on disabled young people, as the government considers how to encourage more young people into work. The charities raised concerns that an imminent review of young people and work could bring in stricter eligibility rules for keeping disability benefits – or remove them altogether – as part of a wider plan to boost flagging youth job rates. Nearly 1 million 16- to 24-year-olds in the UK are classed as Neet (not in employment, education or training). In their joint letter to the review head and the work and pensions secretary, charity leaders warn cutting support or bringing in sanctions risks pushing thousands of vulnerable youngsters deeper into poverty and further away from employment. The charities fear that a previous proposal for the health element of universal credit to be removed for under-22s with a disability, saving around £300m a year, may be resurrected. However, an analysis by the charity Scope suggests about half of households with an under-22 receiving the universal credit health element are already in poverty, which it said could rise to more than nine in 10 if support was removed. About 184,000 young people aged 16-24 receive the universal credit health element. Charities say this is a cohort with multiple complex physical and mental health needs, not mild conditions. The letter says: 'Change is needed. But this must be built around the principles of support and opportunity, rather than the failed punitive approaches of the past. Evidence shows that cutting benefits worsens health and deepens poverty, while strict conditionality and sanctions is particularly counterproductive and harmful for disabled people.' The charities challenge claims that social security budgets are out of control, pointing out that spending on working-age benefits will remain flat as a percentage of GDP. A director at Action for Children said: 'Cutting benefits or ramping up sanctions will simply drive up poverty and push young people further away from work. If ministers want better outcomes for disabled young people, the evidence points to earlier intervention, tailored support and meaningful job and volunteering opportunities, not sanctions or cuts.' Whitehall sources said no decision had been made on the proposal. The issue was being looked at as part of the review. A government spokesperson said: 'We want to see the potential of young people up and down this country fully realised, whether that be through education, training or work. We are pushing ahead with the biggest youth employment reforms in a generation.'
translation: 英国40多家主要慈善机构警告部长们，不要对残疾年轻人实施更严厉的福利制裁或削减，因为政府正考虑如何鼓励更多年轻人就业。这些慈善机构担心，即将进行的年轻人与就业审查可能会收紧保留残疾福利的资格规则，甚至完全取消，作为提振低迷的年轻人就业率更广泛计划的一部分。英国约有近100万名16至24岁的人被归为 NEET（未就业、未受教育或未接受培训）。在给审查负责人和就业与养老金大臣的联名信中，慈善机构领导人警告，削减支持或引入制裁有可能把数千名弱势年轻人更深地推入贫困、推离就业。慈善机构担心，此前一项提议——取消22岁以下残障人士的通用信贷健康部分，每年节省约3亿英镑——可能会被重新提起。然而，慈善机构 Scope 的分析显示，领取通用信贷健康部分的22岁以下人士所在家庭中，约一半已处于贫困之中；如果取消支持，这一比例可能升至十分之九以上。约18.4万名16至24岁年轻人领取通用信贷健康部分。慈善机构表示，这是一个有多种复杂身心需求的人群，而非轻症。联名信写道：变革是需要的，但必须建立在支持与机会的原则之上，而非过去失败的惩罚性做法。证据表明，削减福利会恶化健康、加深贫困，而对残障人士来说，严格的条件限制和制裁尤其适得其反、有害。慈善机构反驳了社会保障预算失控的说法，指出劳动年龄福利支出在议会剩余任期内占 GDP 的比重将保持平稳。儿童行动组织一位主管说：削减福利或加强制裁只会推高贫困，把年轻人推离工作更远。如果部长们想为残疾年轻人取得更好的结果，证据指向更早干预、量身定制的支持以及有意义的就业和志愿服务机会，而非制裁或削减。
summary: 40多家慈善机构联名反对削减残疾年轻人福利，警告制裁将加深贫困、推远就业，呼吁支持而非惩罚。

title: GCSE results: almost one in four boys in England get top grades in maths
content: Almost one in four boys in England received top grades in maths while results in English improved across the board, helping to propel improved GCSE results for this year's cohort of 16-year-olds. The stronger performances in maths helped pupils taking GCSEs in year 11 reach a record level for higher grades in England outside the Covid pandemic years, when exams were replaced by teacher assessments. The overall results for 16-year-olds nudged slightly higher compared with last year, with the proportion receiving grades 7, 8 and 9 – equivalent to grades A and A* – rising by 0.1 of a percentage point to 23.1%. The proportion of nearly 700,000 16-year-olds in England who got a grade 4 or better – equivalent to a C or higher – also rose to 70.7%, compared with 70.5% in 2025. Some of the strongest performances appeared to come in the compulsory subject of maths, where 22.3% received 7s or better, including 24% of boys and 20.5% of girls. But girls did worse than last year in lower grades, dropping from 71% awarded 4 and above to 70.7%, while boys improved further to 72.8%. In English, the other compulsory subject, results bounced back after dipping last year, with 66.1% of boys getting 4s and above while girls improved to 76.8%. Many of the pupils receiving GCSE results this summer were in year 5 when schools were largely closed due to Covid-19 restrictions, disrupting their final years of primary schooling. The general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders said it should be remembered that these young people experienced significant disruption earlier in their education. That so many have done so well in their GCSEs is an example of triumph over adversity both for them and for their schools. However, a significant proportion of students continue to fall short of a grade 4 GCSE pass in English and maths both at the age of 16 and in subsequent resits. This limits their education and career options and is very likely to be a factor in the large number of young people who end up not in employment, education or training. The results came as more than a million candidates in England, Wales and Northern Ireland received their grades on Thursday morning. Twenty-two per cent of UK entries were awarded the top grades this year, up by 0.1 percentage points on last year.
translation: 英格兰近四分之一的男孩在数学上获得最高分，而英语成绩全面提高，推动今年16岁考生的 GCSE 成绩提升。数学方面的强劲表现帮助11年级参加 GCSE 的学生，在英格兰达到除新冠疫情期间（考试被教师评估取代）之外的更高分数纪录。16岁考生的总体成绩与去年相比小幅上升，获得7、8、9分（相当于 A 和 A*）的比例上升0.1个百分点至23.1%。英格兰近70万名16岁考生中，获得4分或以上（相当于 C 或更高）的比例也升至70.7%，高于2025年的70.5%。最强劲的表现似乎出现在必修科目数学上，22.3%的考生获得7分或以上，其中男孩24%、女孩20.5%。但女孩在较低分数上比去年差，获得4分及以上的比例从71%降至70.7%，而男孩进一步升至72.8%。在另一门必修科目英语中，成绩在去年下滑后反弹，66.1%的男孩获得4分及以上，女孩升至76.8%。今夏领取 GCSE 成绩的许多学生，在小学基本因新冠封锁停课时还在读五年级，这打乱了他们小学最后几年的学业。学校与学院领袖协会总书记说，应记住这些年轻人在早期教育中经历了重大干扰。这么多人在 GCSE 和其他二级资格考试中表现如此出色，是学生和学校战胜逆境的例证。然而，相当一部分学生无论在16岁还是之后的补考中，仍达不到英语和数学 GCSE 4分及格线。这限制了他们的教育和职业选择，很可能也是大量年轻人最终陷入 NEET 状态的因素之一。
summary: 英格兰 GCSE 成绩小幅上升，数学表现尤其亮眼（近四分之一男孩获高分），但补考及格率低仍是隐忧。

title: Compulsory GCSE resits in England harm teenagers' mental wellbeing, study finds
content: Forcing teenagers who fail GCSEs into multiple resits has a negative impact on their mental health, according to research to be published as pupils receive their grades on Thursday. The study by academics at University College London compared the mental wellbeing of students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland who failed to reach a grade 4 in maths or English GCSEs – and found that only those in England, where resits are mandatory, showed significantly lower wellbeing. Robbie Maris, a research fellow at UCL and one of the authors, said the dent to teenagers' self-confidence when faced with resits could be a contributing factor to the rise in young people not in education, employment or training. Maris said: 'Some resitting students will not turn up for their exams, they won't enter them or they will drop out of education – these are the kids at highest risk of dropping out of education. It could be leading to further disengagement, which is a worrying thing. People need to pay more attention to this, because if you demotivate or demoralise young people it puts them at risk of dropping out of the education system entirely.' The resits policy in England was introduced in 2014 and requires students who have not achieved a grade 4 pass in English or maths GCSE at age 16 to continue to study those qualifications as a condition of their further education places being funded. This year, about 180,000 students will retake GCSE English and about 175,000 are expected to retake maths. Maris said the comparison between students with similar academic records in Wales and Northern Ireland and those in England, after adjusting for other factors, left the resits policy as a major difference between the two groups. 'We see no impact really at all for failing English and maths in Wales or Northern Ireland but in England there's a relatively large negative impact. This is strong evidence that it's something to do with England's policy setting that is generating these impacts.' The study also found considerable differences between girls and boys. The biggest impact on girls was on those who narrowly missed out on a grade 4 in maths, while for boys the biggest impact was among those who were substantially below the threshold for a passing grade in English. The mandatory resits policy has been controversial since its introduction, with the success rate among 17- to 19-year-olds falling in recent years.
translation: 根据一项将在周四学生领取成绩时发表的研究，强制未通过 GCSE 的青少年反复补考对他们的心理健康有负面影响。伦敦大学学院学者的这项研究比较了英格兰、威尔士和北爱尔兰在数学或英语 GCSE 未达4分学生的心理健康状况，发现只有强制补考的英格兰学生心理健康明显更低。该研究作者之一、UCL 研究员罗比·马里什表示，面对补考时青少年自信受挫，可能是 NEET（未就业、未受教育或未接受培训）年轻人增加的一个促成因素。马里什说：一些补考学生不会出现在考场上，不会报名，或者干脆辍学——这些是流失教育风险最高的孩子。这可能导致进一步脱节，这是令人担忧的事。人们需要更加关注这一点，因为如果让年轻人失去动力、士气低落，他们就有完全脱离教育体系的风险。英格兰的补考政策于2014年推出，要求16岁时英语或数学 GCSE 未获4分的学生继续学习这些课程，作为其继续教育或学院名额获得资助的条件。今年，约18万名学生将重考 GCSE 英语，约17.5万预计重考数学。马里什说，在调整其他因素后，比较威尔士、北爱尔兰与英格兰学业记录相似的学生，补考政策成为两组之间最大的差异。我们在威尔士或北爱尔兰完全看不到英语数学不及格的负面影响，但在英格兰有相对较大的负面影响。这是强有力的证据，表明是英格兰的政策设定造成了这些影响。该研究还发现男女差异显著：女孩受数学差一点不及格影响最大，男孩则受英语远低于及格线影响最大。自推出以来，强制补考政策一直备受争议，17至19岁年龄组的成功率近年不断下降。
summary: UCL 研究对比三国数据发现，英格兰强制 GCSE 补考显著损害青少年心理健康，或加剧 NEET 现象。

title: 'Our children are less cognitively capable,' says neuroscientist who wants to cut screen use in schools
content: Jared Cooney Horvath is on a mission. In the wake of global campaigns for smartphone bans in schools, the neuroscientist wants to raise the alarm about educational technology in classrooms. A former teacher, Horvath believes the use of screens and digital tools in schools is undermining how children learn and develop. 'This might be one of the hardest truths our generation has to face,' he writes in his book, The Digital Delusion. 'Our children are less cognitively capable than we were at their age. For nearly two centuries, the west experienced steady generational progress. Each new cohort of children grew up, on average, healthier, happier, and better educated than the last. Until now.' Starting around the year 2000, something changed. 'Across the west, IQ scores began to fall – even as time spent in school kept rising,' writes Horvath. Scores in international tests started to drop. Why? 'The answer lies in the meteoric rise of educational technology.' The UK educational technology market generated an annual turnover of about £6.5bn. In the US, Horvath says it is a $400bn mega-industry, woven into every aspect of schooling. 'We've been making some incredible strides on the screen-based childhood stuff which even two years ago, I did not think was going to happen as fast as it did,' he said. 'But it's not just about getting rid of screens for entertainment. It's about reducing them as much as possible for academic learning as well if we want our kids to have deep transferrable knowledge.' The uptake of laptops in schools began in earnest in 2010-12, Horvath said, but it was when Covid hit a decade later that every school had to pivot digital as a Band-Aid. 'But when Covid finished you would assume they'd rip that Band-Aid off, but the vast majority of schools didn't. They just stayed digital.' He cites recent scores from the programme for international student assessment (Pisa). In 2012, 2015 and 2018, Pisa asked students how much time they spent using digital devices during a typical school day. 'The more time students spent on screens at school, the further their scores fell. On average, those who used computers for more than six hours per day scored 66 points lower than their peers who didn't use them at all.' Others working in the field are concerned about the risks of confusing correlation with causation. An emerita professor at UCL said moderate school device use is associated with better results than no school device use. It's just that the heaviest daily use is the worst.
translation: 贾里德·库尼·霍瓦特肩负使命。在全球各地发起校园智能手机禁令和16岁以下社交媒体限制运动之际，这位神经科学家想就课堂上的教育技术敲响警钟。霍瓦特曾是教师，他认为屏幕和数字工具在学校的使用正在损害孩子的学习和发展。他在新书《数字错觉》中写道：这可能是我们这一代人必须面对的最艰难真相之一。他说：我们的孩子在认知能力上不如我们同龄时。近两个世纪以来，西方经历了稳定的代际进步。每一代新成长起来的孩子平均都比上一代更健康、更快乐、受教育程度更高。直到现在。大约从2000年开始，有些事情变了。霍瓦特写道：在整个西方，智商分数开始下降——即便在校时间持续上升。国际测试分数开始下滑。为什么？答案在于教育技术的飞速崛起。英国教育技术市场的年营业额约为65亿英镑。在美国，霍瓦特说这是一个4000亿美元的巨型产业，渗透到教育的方方面面。他说：我们在屏幕化童年问题上取得了令人难以置信的进展，即便两年前我还没想到会这么快。但问题不只是把屏幕从娱乐中拿走。如果我们希望孩子拥有深入、可迁移的知识，也要尽可能把屏幕从学业学习中拿走。霍瓦特说，学校配备笔记本电脑始于2010-12年，但十年后疫情来袭时，每所学校都不得不把数字化作为权宜之计。但疫情结束后你会以为他们会撕掉这张创可贴，绝大多数学校却没有，他们只是继续数字化。他引用国际学生评估项目（Pisa）的最新分数。2012、2015和2018年，Pisa 询问学生在一个典型上学日使用数字设备的时间。学生在学校屏幕前花的时间越多，分数下降得越厉害。平均而言，每天用电脑超过六小时的学生比完全不用电脑的同学低66分。该领域的其他专家则担心混淆相关与因果的风险。UCL 一位荣休教授表示，适度的校内设备使用与比完全不用更好的成绩相关，只是最重的日常使用最糟糕。
summary: 神经科学家霍瓦特主张减少校园屏幕使用，称孩子认知能力下降；但专家提醒警惕把相关当因果。

structure.summary: 屏幕与教育技术损害学习，孩子认知能力下降
Pisa 数据显示每天用屏超6小时分数低66分
专家提醒相关非因果，适度使用或比不用更好

hard.s: It's not just about getting rid of screens for entertainment. It's about reducing them as much as possible for academic learning as well if we want our kids to have deep transferrable knowledge.
hard.t: 问题不只是把屏幕从娱乐中拿走。如果我们希望孩子拥有深入、可迁移的知识，也要尽可能把屏幕从学业学习中拿走。

title: 'I'm going for a few pints now': nerves and joy as students collect their A-level results
content: There are few days that teenagers dread more than A-level results day, where students learn how the last two years of their lives will shape their futures, communicated through a few letters in an envelope. The tension of walking into college to learn your fate is enough to keep most people awake the night before. For Hayden Bettson-Day, 18, the best solution was get it over with as early as possible. 'I was refreshing the Ucas page at 8 o'clock in the morning, waiting for it to go on. So, it was a definite bit of tension. My mum kept asking: What is it? What did you get?' What Hayden got was an A* in maths coupled with two As in chemistry and biology, which is enough to be accepted into Newcastle University to study medicine. Aidan Chiu and Fran Whitehead, two of Hayden's classmates, spoke about their own relief at their results, having both received A*s in chemistry. 'My mum's on the phone to Bristol University,' said Aidan, who plans to study maths. 'I have the grades I need, but she's still calling them to make sure I got in. I can't believe it.' Fran, who will now study geology at the University of Exeter, said that the last two years had been difficult, but praised the college for helping her settle and supporting her during such a pivotal time in her life. 'I came to this school knowing nobody, but all the teachers and students were really nice and I found my place. You've got lots of support to achieve your potential.' Not every student was as optimistic, with some planning to go through clearing or committing themselves to return to sixth form to achieve the grades they desired. In Natalia Ntabola's case, the plan was more straightforward: 'If I didn't get into university, I was just going to move out of the country and live somewhere off the grid, to be honest.' Luckily for Natalia, she and lifelong best friend Sandra Konarska, both 18, got the grades that the pair needed in order to attend the University of Manchester together. Michael Fitzsimons, the principal of Trinity sixth form academy, attributes the college's success to the ethics of hard work and commitment, but also stresses the sixth form's commitment to bringing in students from all backgrounds and abilities. To get their students ready for the realities of life, the college funds a scholars programme to give high achieving students free access to tutors from some of the country's top universities. Now, with the tension of the morning relieved, the students are celebrating in a variety of ways. The majority, as expected, have set off for the pubs in Halifax town centre, including Hayden. 'I'm going for a few pints now,' he said. 'I'm going to Newcastle for the next few years and I've heard about the nightlife, so I need to start practising.'
translation: 很少有日子比 A-level 放榜日更让青少年恐惧——学生们通过信封里的几个字母得知过去两年如何塑造他们的未来。走进学校得知自己命运的那份紧张，足以让大多数人在前一晚失眠。对18岁的海登·贝特森-戴来说，最好的解决办法是尽早了断。他说：我早上8点就在刷新 Ucas 页面，等着它上线，确实有点紧张。我妈妈一直问：怎么样？考了多少？海登考了数学 A* 加化学、生物两个 A，足以被纽卡斯尔大学医学院录取。他的两名同学艾丹·周和弗兰·怀特黑德谈到了得知成绩后的如释重负，两人都拿到化学 A*。计划学数学的艾丹说：我妈妈正给布里斯托大学打电话。我拿到了需要的成绩，但她还是打电话确认我有没有被录取。我不敢相信。将赴埃克塞特大学学地质学的弗兰说，过去两年很艰难，但她赞扬学院帮助她安定下来，在她人生的关键时刻支持她适应新环境。我来到这所学校时谁都不认识，但所有老师和学生都很好，我找到了自己的位置。你有大量支持去实现自己的潜能。并非每个学生都对自己的成绩那么乐观，有些人计划走补录流程，或决定重回六年级考取理想的成绩。对纳塔利娅·恩塔博拉来说，计划更直接：说实话，如果我没考上大学，我就搬出这个国家，去一个与世隔绝的地方生活。幸运的是，她和终身挚友桑德拉·科纳尔斯卡都拿到了两人所需的成绩，可以一起进入曼彻斯特大学。特里尼蒂六年级学院的校长迈克尔·菲茨西蒙斯将学院的成功归功于努力与承诺的校风，同时强调学院致力于招收各种背景和能力的学生。我们绝不想让人为我们的孩子感到遗憾。我们这里的不利条件大约是其他地区的两倍，但这不会改变期望。我们仍对他们寄予高期望，不过这种期望是充满爱地传达的。
summary: A-level 放榜日：学生们紧张领取成绩，有人如愿以偿，有人走补录；一所学院用努力与支持帮助学生成长。

structure.summary: 海登等学生紧张查分，如愿获大学录取
有人庆祝有人走补录，挚友携手同入曼大
高期望加关爱，学者计划助寒门学生自信

hard.s: There are few days that teenagers dread more than A-level results day, where students learn how the last two years of their lives will shape their futures.
hard.t: 很少有日子比 A-level 放榜日更让青少年恐惧——学生们通过几个字母得知过去两年如何塑造他们的未来。
hard.a: few...more than 为否定比较，意为几乎没有比…更；where 定语从句修饰 day；shape 意为塑造。

title: 'It's easy to slip into the negatives': students on their biggest financial shocks
content: We asked students, and recent graduates, to tell us about the biggest financial shock they had when they started university, and what advice they had for freshers. George Gribben, third year, University of Brighton. Biggest shock: the price of public transport is ridiculous. I pay the same price back home in Switzerland, but the trains and buses are actually on time. I want to visit my best friend, who goes to university in Exeter, but it's £90 to get there. Advice: get into cycling: buying a secondhand bike is cheaper in the long run than all of the bus and train tickets. And try to befriend people who have cars. Elodie Clements, master's, LSE. Biggest shock: moving to London from a rural part of West Yorkshire I knew it was very expensive, but I didn't realise just how big the margin between spending at home, versus at university, would be until I was doing my weekly shop and getting the tube. Advice: track your spending weekly as well as monthly. It's easiest to do this by opening another bank account and transferring a weekly allowance into it. Charlotte Farrow, third year, University of Brighton. Biggest shock: the rent in the second year. The quality of my house was poor – mould, leaks and a faulty washing machine. It was £700 a month, without bills. It definitely gave me a reality check. Advice: there's no harm in being proactive: you'll know people looking for houses as early as the November before. Jess Mallaghan, 2026 graduate, Loughborough University. Biggest shock: how many people received an allowance, or financial support, from their parents. A lot of the more sheltered students really struggled as they had never had to budget or cook before. Advice: split your student finance by month. Allocate a certain amount every month. If you can, have a small reserve. I made the mistake of not worrying about money during freshers' week and, by January, I was struggling. Mathonwy Akuwimi, third year, University of Leicester. Biggest shock: the day-to-day cost of maintaining a healthy balanced diet. I realised how expensive everyday essentials were becoming. Advice: budget carefully from the start, and shop at places such as Aldi or Lidl to help keep costs under control. Farryn Stock, graduate. Biggest shock: the equipment and software they expected everyone to pay for. Before the course, they told us we would need Adobe software downloaded. I hadn't even written my first article before forking out a grand. Advice: something that really helped me was a student account with an interest-free overdraft, perfect if you're ever in a tight spot one month. Charlotte Smith, 2026 graduate. Biggest shock: early on in my degree, I opened an overdraft as a safety net. I was shocked at how easy and common it is to slip into the negatives. Advice: invest some time in creating a budget tracker that works for you – and refrain from offering to buy a round with money that you may need to pay the bills.
translation: 我们请学生和刚毕业的人谈谈他们上大学时最大的财务冲击，以及对新生的建议。布莱顿大学大三学生乔治·格里本：最大的冲击是公共交通的价格荒谬。我在瑞士家乡付同样的价格，但火车和公交都准时。我想去看在埃克塞特上大学的好朋友，但要花90英镑。建议：开始骑车吧，长远看二手自行车比所有公交火车票都便宜。还要试着结交有车的人。伦敦政经硕士生埃洛迪·克莱门茨：最大的冲击是从西约克郡乡村搬到伦敦，我知道很贵，但没意识到家里和大学花销的差距有多大，直到每周采购和坐地铁时才明白。建议：按周也按月追踪支出。最简单的方法是另开一个银行账户，每周转入零花钱。布莱顿大学大三学生夏洛特·法罗：最大的冲击是第二年的房租。我住的房子质量很差——发霉、漏水、洗衣机坏了。每月700英镑还不含账单。这绝对给我敲了警钟。建议：主动一点没坏处，11月前就会有人找合租了。拉夫堡大学2026届毕业生杰丝·马拉根：最大的冲击是有多少人从父母那里拿零用钱或经济支持。许多被保护得很好的学生真的挣扎，因为他们从没做过预算或做过饭。建议：把学生贷款按月分配，每月留出一定数额。如果可能，留一点储备金。迎新周时我犯了个错误——不操心钱，到一月就捉襟见肘了。莱斯特大学大三学生马索努·阿库维米：最大的冲击是维持健康均衡饮食的日常成本。我意识到日常必需品越来越贵，光吃好就很花钱。建议：一开始就仔细做预算，去 Aldi 或 Lidl 这样的超市控制成本。创意艺术大学毕业生法琳·斯托克：最大的冲击是他们期望每个人都为设备和软件付钱。开课前他们就说我们需要装 Adobe 软件，还没写第一篇文章就先花了一千英镑。建议：学生账户带免息透支真的帮了我，如果某个月手头紧就派上用场。
summary: 在校生和毕业生分享大学财务冲击：交通、房租、伙食、设备成本远超预期，建议做预算、骑车、学会做饭。

structure.summary: 公共交通价高，二手房东第二年起跳涨，质量参差
日常必需品昂贵，健康饮食成本高，家长补贴差距明显
按月预算、留储备、免息透支应急，避免陷入负数

hard.s: I didn't realise just how big the margin between spending at home, versus at university, would be until I was doing my weekly shop and getting the tube.
hard.t: 我没意识到家里和大学花销的差距有多大，直到每周采购和坐地铁时才明白。
hard.a: not...until 意为直到…才；the margin between 意为…之间的差距；versus 意为与…相比。

title: Premier League: nine newcomers to watch in the top flight this season
content: Newcastle, Arsenal, Brentford, Everton, Leeds, Coventry, Aston Villa, Hull and Ipswich have all brought in exciting players this summer. Bazoumana Touré: Newcastle. Anthony Gordon will be a difficult act to follow at Newcastle, but Touré could be a shrewd replacement. Blessed with electric pace, the 20-year-old is a bit more of an old-fashioned winger in that he predominantly plays from the left and is left-footed. As a result, he was more of a creator than a goalscorer for Hoffenheim last season. Of his 14 Bundesliga goal involvements last term, nine were assists. Christos Tzolis: Arsenal. While hardly the most glamorous name, Leandro Trossard was a useful and dependable player for Arsenal. Replacing him is easier said than done. Tzolis has been given that task and he looks a good fit. For starters, he was a highly effective creator for Club Brugge last season, with his 135 chances created being 35 more than anyone else in the Belgian league. Mamadou Sangaré: Brentford. There are plenty of French football experts who were very surprised to see Sangaré only end up at Brentford this summer. The fact the Mali international has just a single season's experience in a top league may have counted against him, though Brentford look set to benefit from the hesitance of others. Hayden Hackney: Everton. Hackney built a strong reputation during his four full seasons in the Championship with Middlesbrough. Hackney is a deep-lying playmaker who is accurate in possession but also brings a degree of progressiveness with his passing. Caleb Yirenkyi: Coventry. The 20-year-old Ghana international has been exciting people in analytics circles for a while thanks to his broad skill set. Nominally a central midfielder, Yirenkyi can feature as a No 6, a No 8 or even at right-back. Emersonn: Ipswich. The last time Ipswich were in the Premier League they put faith in a young centre-forward. They're doing so again, having spent £24m on the Brazilian striker Emersonn from Toulouse. He scored only six times in 28 league appearances last season. But he should still offer plenty. Johan Manzambi: Aston Villa. The 20-year-old is a forward-thinking midfielder who is capable of bursting forward and evading opponents in tight spaces. He then impressed at the World Cup. Lucas Herrington: Hull. He did not make his debut until February, but was still named to the MLS All-Star squad after his first World Cup campaign with Australia. The 18-year-old's rise has been rapid. Tarik Muharemovic: Leeds. Leeds made Muharemovic their second-most expensive signing when they paid £34m this summer. The Bosnia and Herzegovina international has technical ability and is also a unit and strong competitor.
translation: 纽卡斯尔、阿森纳、布伦特福德、埃弗顿、利兹、考文垂、阿斯顿维拉、赫尔和伊普斯维奇今夏都引入了令人兴奋的球员。巴祖马纳·图雷：纽卡斯尔。安东尼·戈登在纽卡斯尔很难被替代，但图雷可能是精明的替代者。这位20岁小将拥有电光般的速度，更像传统边锋，主要从左侧发起进攻且惯用左脚。因此上赛季他在霍芬海姆更多是创造者而非得分手。上赛季14次德甲进球参与中，9次是助攻。克里斯托斯·佐利斯：阿森纳。虽然莱安德罗·特罗萨德不是最耀眼的球员，但他是阿森纳有用而可靠的球员。替代他说来容易做来难。佐利斯被委以重任，看起来非常合适。首先，他上赛季是布鲁日俱乐部的高效创造者，创造135次机会，比比利时联赛其他人多35次。马马杜·桑加雷：布伦特福德。许多法国足球专家非常惊讶桑加雷今夏最终只去了布伦特福德。这位马里国脚只有单赛季顶级联赛经验，这可能是他减分的原因，不过布伦特福德看起来将受益于其他球队的犹豫。海登·哈克尼：埃弗顿。哈克尼在米德尔斯堡四个完整英冠赛季中建立了良好声誉。他是一名拖后组织核心，控球精准，传球也带有一定的向前推进性。卡莱布·伊伦基：考文垂。这位20岁的加纳国脚凭借全面的技能早已让数据分析圈兴奋不已。名义上是中场中路球员，伊伦基可以踢6号、8号甚至右后卫。埃默森：伊普斯维奇。伊普斯维奇上次在英超时信任年轻中锋，这次又这么做了，花了2400万英镑从图卢兹签下巴西前锋埃默森。他上赛季28次联赛出场仅入6球，但仍应带来很多东西。约翰·曼赞比：阿斯顿维拉。这位20岁球员是向前思考型中场，能够突进并在狭小空间摆脱对手。他随后在世界杯上表现出色。卢卡斯·赫林顿：赫尔。他到2月才完成首秀，但随澳大利亚打完首次世界杯后入选了美职联全明星阵容。这位18岁小将的崛起十分迅速。塔里克·穆哈雷莫维奇：利兹。利兹今夏花3400万英镑签下穆哈雷莫维奇，这是他当时第二贵的签约。这位波黑国脚技术出色，而且体格强壮、竞争意识强。
summary: 英超新赛季九名值得关注的新援盘点：从纽卡斯尔的电光边锋到赫尔18岁天才中卫，各家补强各有亮点。

title: Football transfer rumours: Newcastle to sign Manchester City's Nico González?
content: A Manchester City clearout is in the offing, which could aid Newcastle's search for a new central midfielder to replace the departed Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães. Nico González could be packing his bags to head up to St James' Park, having never quite proven himself at the Etihad Stadium. Attacking players Omar Marmoush and Savinho, meanwhile, are on their way to Tottenham, which should kickstart a busy end to the window at City. On the other side of Manchester, United are looking to sell off some of their younger players to Arsenal. The Gibraltar international James Scanlon and Habeeb Ogunneye are set for moves to the Premier League champions. The Gunners are ramping up their recruitment of young players to strengthen quality across the club. On his way out of the Emirates Stadium is another youngster, with Ethan Nwaneri wanted by Fulham and Everton, while RB Leipzig could also come into the mix for a loan move. Gabriel Jesus has also been linked with an exit but the Brazilian wants to stick around at the Emirates. Ezri Konsa is on his way to Arsenal, so Unai Emery needs a replacement. One man on the radar is the Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo, who is surplus to requirements, but Marseille may compete for his signature. It is hard to keep up with Aston Villa's antics at the moment, so Ajax engaging them in talks over a potential move for Leon Bailey may have been missed by the less discerning rumour mongers. The Jamaica international has a year remaining on his deal at Villa Park. It may not seem like Everton are getting much done, but they are supposedly working on things in the background. In addition to Nwaneri, Como's Assane Diao is a winger attracting their attention and a bid could be made for the Ivorian – but with a potential £60m price tag, whether it comes to anything is unlikely. Hectic Hull are set to miss out Niccolo Fortini after his club, Fiorentina, agreed a deal with Torino. The blow may be softened if they can get a deal over the line for Nottingham Forest's Dilane Bakwa. Crystal Palace cannot afford to sell any of their key players but Galatasaray have called up with an offer for Ismaïla Sarr, which was quickly rejected. Championship side Wrexham are trying to ramp up their summer transfer business with a move for Plymouth's Bim Pepple but could face competition from Preston for the striker.
translation: 曼城正在酝酿一场大清洗，这可能有助于纽卡斯尔寻找新中场，以替代离队的桑德罗·托纳利和布鲁诺·吉马良斯。尼科·冈萨雷斯可能收拾行囊前往圣詹姆斯公园，他在伊蒂哈德球场始终没能证明自己。与此同时，攻击手马尔穆什和萨维尼奥将前往热刺，这应会开启曼城繁忙的转会窗尾声。曼彻斯特另一边，曼联打算把一些年轻球员卖给阿森纳。直布罗陀国脚詹姆斯·斯坎伦和哈比卜·奥贡内耶即将转会英超卫冕冠军。枪手正加紧招募年轻球员以增强全队实力。又一名年轻人即将离开酋长球场，富勒姆和埃弗顿都想要伊桑·恩瓦内里，而 RB 莱比锡也可能加入租借谈判。加布里埃尔·热苏斯也传出离队传闻，但这位巴西人想留在酋长球场。孔萨即将加盟阿森纳，所以乌奈·埃梅里需要替代者。雷达上一个名字是切尔西后卫托辛·阿达拉比奥约，他已是多余之人，但马赛可能争夺他的签约。目前很难跟上阿斯顿维拉的动作，所以阿贾克斯正与他们就莱昂·贝利潜在转会进行谈判，这件事可能被不那么敏锐的八卦者错过。这位牙买加国脚在维拉公园的合同还剩一年。埃弗顿看起来没怎么动作，但据说他们在幕后推进。除了恩瓦内里，科莫的边锋迪奥吸引着他们的注意，可能为这位科特迪瓦人出价——但考虑到潜在的6000万英镑标价，能否成行很难说。忙碌的赫尔将错过福尔蒂尼，因为他的俱乐部佛罗伦萨已与都灵达成协议。如果能敲定诺丁汉森林巴夸的交易，这一打击或可缓解。水晶宫无力出售任何关键球员，但加拉塔萨雷已就伊萨尔·萨尔的报价打了电话，很快遭到拒绝。英冠球队雷克瑟姆正试图通过引进普利茅斯的佩普尔加速夏季转会，但可能面临普雷斯顿对这名前锋的竞争。
summary: 英超转会窗尾声传闻满天飞：曼城清洗、曼联出售年轻人、维拉找后卫替身、多队抢购新星。

title: Fifth Fifa vice-president turns against Infantino, saying he has 'lost confidence' in him
content: Gianni Infantino has lost the support of another one of Fifa's vice-presidents, with the Hungarian football federation chief, Sandor Csanyi, criticising the president's professional judgment, ethical standards and leadership. In an explosive letter sent to Infantino on Tuesday, which was first obtained by the news agency Agence France-Presse, Csanyi states that he has lost the confidence I previously placed in you and describes the unexpected dismissal of Fifa's chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, as the final straw. Lamour was sacked by Fifa on Monday after breaking ranks last month by criticising Infantino over his aborted plan to sell off shares in the World Cup to private investors. Csanyi's letter continues the trend of senior global football figures deserting Infantino, with the Hungarian banker the fifth of Fifa's eight vice-presidents to call for him to stand down. The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, Victor Montagliani of Concacaf, and Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al Khalifa of the Asian Football Confederation have all made their positions clear, as has the Football Association chair, Debbie Hewitt. Of the Fifa vice-presidents, only Alejandro Domínguez of South America's Conmebol, Patrick Motsepe of the Confederation of African Football and Oceania's Lambert Maltock are supporting Infantino. Csanyi is also a member of the 37-strong Fifa council, which is theoretically its main decision-making body, but has been repeatedly overlooked by Infantino. My conviction that you are capable of continuing to lead Fifa successfully and effectively in accordance with the shared values that previously formed the basis of our cooperation has been undermined, Csanyi wrote. The final straw was the unexpected dismissal of Kevin Lamour. The letter also cited a number of controversial decisions at this year's World Cup, including Infantino's involvement in plans to outsource Fifa competitions and place them in the hands of external parties.
translation: 詹尼·因凡蒂诺又失去了一位国际足联副主席的支持，匈牙利足协主席桑多尔·查尼批评主席的专业判断、道德标准和领导力。在周二发给因凡蒂诺的爆炸性信件中——该信首先由法新社获得——查尼表示自己已失去先前对你的信任，并把国际足联首席运营官凯文·拉莫尔意外被解职描述为压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。拉莫尔周一被国际足联解雇，此前他上个月打破沉默，批评因凡蒂诺搁置的向私人投资者出售世界杯股份的计划。查尼的信延续了全球足坛重量级人物离弃因凡蒂诺的趋势，这位匈牙利银行家成为国际足联八位副主席中第五位呼吁他下台的人。欧足联主席切费林、中北美及加勒比海足联的蒙塔利亚尼以及亚足联的萨尔曼亲王都已表明立场，英足总主席黛比·休伊特亦然。在国际足联副主席中，只有南美足联的多明格斯、非洲足联的莫特塞佩和大洋洲足联的马尔托克支持因凡蒂诺。查尼还是37人组成的国际足联理事会成员，该理事会理论上是主要决策机构，但屡遭因凡蒂诺忽视。查尼写道：你能够按照先前构成我们合作基础的共同价值观，继续成功有效地领导国际足联，我的这一信念已被动摇。压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草是凯文·拉莫尔意外被解职。这封信还列举了今年世界杯上的一系列有争议决定，包括因凡蒂诺参与将国际足联赛事外包、交予外部方手中的计划。
summary: 国际足联八位副主席中第五位倒戈，匈牙利足协主席公开批评因凡蒂诺，要求其下台。

title: London flat where boy fell to death could have had more safeguards, inquest told
content: An inquest into the death of a five-year-old boy who fell from a 15th-floor window has heard that more measures could have been taken to make it safer. Aalim Ahmed, who was autistic, died when he fell from a kitchen window at a residential block in Plaistow, east London. His father rushed from the top floor temporary social housing flat and discovered his body shortly before 6am on 16 May 2024. There was a long history of complaints about the council accommodation from the family, who had asked to be moved, the court heard. East London coroner's court heard that the Newham council property manager thought more restricted features could have been installed after visiting the Ahmed family on the afternoon he died. In a note to the council after seeing the family, the property manager wrote: 'Following the horrible incident and fatality, I visited the family yesterday. The kitchen window from where the child fell off is functional but can be operated by a child, hence the incident. There is a restricted feature to allow a limited opening. More restricted features could have been installed to reduce this risk.' The family had asked to be moved from the block. The parents have described their son's death as preventable and blamed the council, after claims safety concerns about the flat were reported on multiple occasions. A postmortem examination found the boy died from multiple injuries due to or as a consequence of trauma from a fall from height. The mother has told the court she was scared and horrified when the council put them in the top-floor flat, which needed repairs, because her son had no sense of danger. She felt the property was not suitable for her young family, which also included a newborn girl, but felt obliged to take it or risk homelessness. On the day the boy died, one of the first things the mother told the property manager was: 'I asked to be moved and nobody listened to me.' The council property manager said she tried the window twice and was able to open it on the second attempt, but could not remember exactly how she did it. The council said it would be unable to comment until after the inquest concluded. The hearing continues.
translation: 对一名从15楼窗户坠亡的五岁男孩的死因调查听证称，本可以采取更多措施让窗户更安全。患自闭症的阿利姆·艾哈迈德，在从伦敦东部普莱斯托一栋住宅楼的厨房窗户坠落时身亡。2024年5月16日凌晨6点前不久，他的父亲马凯尔·艾哈迈德从顶层临时社会福利住房冲下来，发现了他的尸体。法庭获悉，该家庭对市政会住房有长期投诉史，他们曾要求搬走。东伦敦死因裁判法庭获悉，纽汉市政会物业经理恩嫩纳·穆马在男孩去世当天下午探访艾哈迈德一家后，认为可以安装更多限制性装置。在探访该家庭后给市政会的便条中，物业经理写道：在那场可怕的事件和悲剧发生后，我昨天探访了这家人。孩子坠落的那扇厨房窗户功能正常，但孩子可以操作，因此酿成事故。有一个限制装置允许有限开启。本可以安装更多限制装置来降低这一风险。孩子的父母将他的死描述为可预防的，并归咎于市政会，因为据称安全问题曾多次被报告。尸检发现，男孩死于高处坠落造成的多处创伤。母亲告诉法庭，当市政会把他们安置在需要修缮的顶层公寓时，她又害怕又惊骇，因为儿子没有危险意识。她认为该房产不适合她年幼的家庭，但又觉得不得不接受，否则就要冒无家可归的风险。孩子去世当天，母亲对物业经理说的第一句话是：我要求搬走，但没人听我的。物业经理说她试了两次那扇窗户，第二次打开了，但记不清具体怎么开的。市政会表示在死因调查结束前无法置评。听证仍在继续。
summary: 五岁自闭症男孩从顶层公寓窗户坠亡，死因调查显示本可安装更多限位装置；家庭多次反映安全问题被忽视。
